> Joseph Searle's personal brand and design system: an engineer's notebook printed on paper.

Neptune 1.1 (2026-10-13) is Joseph Searle's personal brand: an engineer's notebook printed on paper. Classical serif for ideas, monospace for anything a machine would say, one electric blue for action. Light paper by default; Deep is the dark theme.

Code, tooling and history live in [JosephSearle/neptune](https://github.com/JosephSearle/neptune): the DTCG token export, `llms.txt` for agents and the CI checks are there, not in the design system page.

Built with:

- Plain CSS: tokens as CSS variables plus `np-` component classes, no framework.
- One small script, `components/neptune.js`, for the interactive components. No dependencies, no build step.
- [Newsreader](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Newsreader) and [IBM Plex Mono](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/IBM+Plex+Mono).
- [W3C Design Tokens](https://www.designtokens.org/) (DTCG 2025.10) export.
- [Playwright](https://playwright.dev/) for visual regression, [stylelint](https://stylelint.io/) for the CSS lint.
- [GitHub Actions](https://docs.github.com/actions) for checks and releases.

## Install

Install a released version from its git tag. Neptune isn't on the npm registry; every release is tagged `vX.Y.Z`.

```bash
npm i github:JosephSearle/neptune#v1.1.0
```

`package.json` then records the tag, so every site shows which version it's on. The install has no dependencies and runs no scripts. It contains only what a site uses: `tokens.css`, `tokens/` (DTCG files and primitives), `components/bundle.css`, `brand/`, `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, the README and the changelog.

### Reference the files

Import by these paths, not by folder:

| Path | File |
| --- | --- |
| `neptune/tokens.css` | `tokens.css` |
| `neptune/bundle.css` | `components/bundle.css` |
| `neptune/neptune.js` | `components/neptune.js`, from the release that adds it |
| `neptune/tokens/*` | DTCG files and primitives, e.g. `neptune/tokens/dtcg/base.tokens.json` |
| `neptune/brand/*` | Logo, favicon set and social card |

With a bundler (Vite, Parcel, webpack, PostCSS with `postcss-import`), import the stylesheets in order:

```css
@import "neptune/tokens.css";
@import "neptune/bundle.css";
```

For plain HTML with no build step, copy the files out of `node_modules/neptune/` into the site's static folder at build or deploy time, and link them as in the [Example](#example):

```bash
cp node_modules/neptune/tokens.css node_modules/neptune/components/bundle.css public/
cp -r node_modules/neptune/brand public/
```

### Upgrade

1. Read the new version's section in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md), or in `node_modules/neptune/CHANGELOG.md` after installing. Check Deprecated and Removed before a major.
2. Change the tag: `npm i github:JosephSearle/neptune#v1.2.0`.
3. Re-copy the files if the site copies them, then check the site at 390px and 1280px in both themes.

### Work on Neptune

To change Neptune itself or run its tooling, clone it and install the dev dependencies:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/JosephSearle/neptune.git
cd neptune
npm ci
```

### Dependencies

- A browser with CSS custom properties and `prefers-color-scheme`.
- JavaScript only for the interactive components: Tabs, Tooltip, Toast, SearchDialog, Dialog, ThemeToggle and CodeCopy need `neptune.js` (ES2017, no dependencies). Every other component is CSS only.
- Google Fonts, imported by `bundle.css`: Newsreader and IBM Plex Mono. Self-host for production.
- Tooling only: Node.js 22 (CI's version) for the token, `llms.txt` and lint scripts and Playwright.
- Brand files only: Python 3 with `fonttools`, `brotli` and `pillow`, for `scripts/build-brand.py`.

## Usage

Load two stylesheets, in this order, plus the fonts and the script:

1. `tokens.css`: every token as a CSS variable, both themes, and a class per type style (`.display`, `.heading`, `.label`…).
2. `components/bundle.css`: the `np-` component classes.
3. Google Fonts: Newsreader (opsz, 300–700, italic) and IBM Plex Mono (400–600). `bundle.css` imports them; self-host for production.
4. `components/neptune.js`, with `defer`, after the stylesheets: `<script src="components/neptune.js" defer></script>`. Only pages with an interactive component need it.

Leave `data-theme` off `<html>` and the page follows the system setting; set `"light"` or `"dark"` when the reader picks one in the ThemeToggle. Wrap the page in `np-root`. Start `<body>` with a SkipLink, then the Nav, then `<main id="main" tabindex="-1">` with its content in `np-container`. Build pages from components: Nav, Hero, SectionHead, Card, Figure, Split, Feed, Table, Prose, CodeCopy, Footer. Docs pages add DocsLayout, Sidebar, Breadcrumb, ArticleHeader, Toc, Pager, Callout and Tabs. Forms use Input, Select, Textarea, Checkbox and Switch. Lay out index pages on PageGrid. Every site gets SearchDialog behind ⌘K and an EmptyState for anything that can come back empty. Feedback uses Toast for results, Dialog for decisions and Tooltip for optional hints; destructive actions go through a Dialog with `np-btn--danger`. Style nothing inline that a component or type class already covers.

### Example

A page with a skip link and a hero, following the system theme:

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="tokens.css">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="components/bundle.css">
  <link rel="icon" href="brand/favicon.svg" type="image/svg+xml">
  <script src="components/neptune.js" defer></script>
</head>
<body class="np-root">
  <a class="np-skip" href="#main">Skip to content</a>
  <main id="main" tabindex="-1" class="np-container">
    <section class="np-hero">
      <span class="np-hero__eyebrow">NEPTUNE / 1.1 · LDN</span>
      <h1 class="np-hero__title">Notes on agents that <em>ship</em>.</h1>
      <p class="np-hero__lead">Playbooks and postmortems.</p>
    </section>
  </main>
</body>
</html>
```

Open it in a browser: a Paper page (Deep if the system is dark) with a serif headline, a mono eyebrow and a skip link that appears on the first Tab. Every component folder has a `preview.html` with working markup to copy.

### Behaviour

`neptune.js` wires components up from their documented markup. Add the markup; there's nothing to call. It runs once per page, however often it's loaded, and nothing it does animates.

| Component | What it wires up |
| --- | --- |
| Tabs | Click selects. Left and Right move and wrap, Home and End go to the first and last. Only the selected tab is in the tab order. |
| Tooltip | Esc hides an open tooltip without moving focus (WCAG 1.4.13); leaving the trigger resets it. The 300ms hover delay is CSS. |
| Toast | Dismiss removes the toast. `Neptune.toast()` adds one with the timing below. |
| SearchDialog | ⌘K / Ctrl+K and the Nav search button open it with `showModal()` and focus the input. Up and Down move `aria-selected`; Enter opens the selected result. |
| Dialog | A button with `data-np-open="id"` opens that dialog with `showModal()`. An input with `data-np-confirm="name"` keeps the form's `np-btn--danger` disabled until the typed text matches. |
| ThemeToggle | Click sets `data-theme` on `<html>`, saves it as `np-theme` in `localStorage` and marks the pressed side; on load, and when the system theme changes, the side the page shows is pressed. |
| CodeCopy | Copy copies the code without `$ ` prompts, then reads "Copied" for 1.5s with `data-copied` set. |

Two functions, on `window.Neptune`:

- `Neptune.init(root)`: sets the initial state (tab order, theme marks, confirm buttons) inside `root`, `document` by default. Call it after adding a Tabs, ThemeToggle or confirm Dialog to the page. Events are delegated, so everything else works without it.
- `Neptune.toast({ kind, label, text, action })`: adds a toast to the page's `np-toasts` region (made if missing) and returns it. `kind` is `"ok"`, `"alert"` or empty for neutral; `action` is `{ label, onClick }`. Ok and neutral toasts leave after 6s, paused while hovered or focused; alerts and toasts with an action stay. At most three show; the oldest goes first.

Chart draws nothing: plot the data and its readout with your own code.

### CLI

The tooling runs through npm scripts:

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run tokens` | Rebuild `tokens/dtcg/` and `tokens.css` from `tokens.json` |
| `npm run llms` | Rebuild `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` |
| `npm run lint` | Lint `components/` for raw colours and `z-index` |
| `npm run contrast` | Measure every documented colour pair in both themes; fail below 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for borders |
| `npm run check` | Everything CI runs, including the install contents check and a syntax check of `neptune.js`; writes nothing |
| `npm run visual` | Screenshot every preview in both themes and compare |
| `npm run a11y` | Run axe-core on every preview in both themes; fail on serious or critical violations |

`python3 scripts/build-brand.py <newsreader-500.woff2>` rebuilds the logo, favicon set and social card from `tokens.json`; [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#making-a-change) has the full command.

### Tokens

`tokens.json` is the source of truth. `scripts/build-tokens.mjs` turns it into W3C DTCG files (format 2025.10) in `tokens/dtcg/`, for Style Dictionary, Terrazzo, Tokens Studio or Figma variables:

- `primitives.tokens.json`: raw colours by family and step (`primitive.blue.600`), from `tokens/primitives.json`.
- `base.tokens.json`: space, radius, stroke, layout, breakpoints, durations, z-index, fonts and type styles. Values DTCG has no type for (`68ch`, `steps(2)`) sit under `$extensions`.
- `paper.tokens.json`, `deep.tokens.json`: the semantic colours and shadow for each theme, as aliases of primitives.

Load primitives + base + one theme. Every semantic colour must alias a primitive: add the primitive first, then use it.

After changing `tokens.json`, `tokens/primitives.json` or `tokens.css`, run `node scripts/build-tokens.mjs`. CI runs it with `--check` and fails if the DTCG files or `tokens.css` disagree with `tokens.json`.

### For agents

`llms.txt` indexes the guide and every component for an LLM, with the rules agents most often break; `llms-full.txt` is the guide and all component READMEs in one file. Both are generated: after changing any README, run `node scripts/build-llms.mjs`. CI fails if they're stale.

### States

Buttons and fields share one set of states. Use the attribute, not a class:

| State | Button | Input, Select, Textarea |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Disabled | `disabled`, or `aria-disabled="true"` on a link with no `href` | `disabled`; box sinks to `paper-sunk` |
| Busy | `aria-busy="true"` plus `disabled`; a block cursor blinks after the label | — |
| Read-only | — | `readonly`; `paper-sunk`, still focusable |
| Invalid | — | `aria-invalid="true"` + `aria-describedby`; border, prompt and hint turn `alert` |

## Voice

- Write direct and terse. Short sentences. No filler ("simply", "in order to", "please note").
- Use the imperative for instructions and UI copy: "Read the playbook", not "You can read the playbook".
- Describe what a thing does, not how good it is. No marketing adjectives.
- Write errors as what went wrong, then what to do: "Build failed: missing `API_BASE_URL`. Set it in `.env`."
- Sentence case for headings. UPPERCASE only in mono labels.
- No emoji. Use the glyph set below instead.

### System metadata

Treat every page like a running program. Stamp it with mono metadata in `meta` style, `ink-muted`:

- Version and place: `NEPTUNE / 1.1 · LDN`
- Dates in ISO: `2026-10-13`
- Indexes on cards and sections: `01`, `02`, `03`
- Status in brackets: `[ SHIPPED ]`, `[ DRAFT ]`, `[ ARCHIVED ]`

Keep it true. A stamp that lies (fake version numbers, fake uptime) is decoration; cut it.

## Colour

- Set every page on `paper`. Raise cards, inputs and keys onto `paper-raised`. Recess code spans and footers into `paper-sunk`.
- Set text in `ink`; metadata and captions in `ink-muted`.
- Spend `neptune` on one thing per view: the primary action, a link, the active nav item, or the focus ring. Never as a large background except the hero block on the cover.
- Put `neptune` text on `neptune-soft` for accent tags and selections. Put `on-neptune` on a `neptune` fill.
- Draw meaningful borders (inputs, cards, tags, kbd) in `line-strong`. Use `line` only for decorative rules.
- Use `ok` and `alert` for state, always with a word or the `np-dot`. Never colour alone.
- Fill `alert` only for the danger button, with `on-alert` text.
- Charts take their own palette, `viz-`: six series hues in a fixed order led by `neptune`, a one-hue sequential ramp and a gold–blue diverging pair. The one-blue rule doesn't apply inside a plot. Chart has the rules; the numbers are measured there.
- Terminals, code blocks, toasts and tooltips stay dark in both themes: `term-bg` with `term-ink`, `term-muted` for prompts, `term-accent` for commands and actions, `term-ok` and `term-alert` for state.

## Type

- Headlines and body in Newsreader (`--font-serif`). Labels, buttons, nav, metadata and code in IBM Plex Mono (`--font-mono`).
- Hero: `display-xl`, once per page. Page title: `display`. Sections: `heading`. Cards: `title`.
- Reading text: `body`, max 68ch. Card copy: `body-sm`. Pull quotes: `quote`. Italic appears only there and on one emphasised word in a Hero title.
- Mono labels: `label`, uppercase, 0.08em tracking. Stamps: `meta`. Code: `code`.
- Never set paragraphs in mono. Never set buttons in serif.

## Space and shape

- Build on a 4px grid: `space-1` to `space-16`. Card padding `space-6`; gap between cards `space-8`; sections `space-16` on desktop, `space-12` on phones.
- Square by default: `radius-none` on cards, tags and terminals; `radius-sm` (2px) on buttons, inputs and keys; `radius-full` only on status dots and radio buttons.
- Every border is `stroke-hairline` (1px). The kbd bottom edge and focus ring are `stroke-key` (2px).
- No blurred shadows. Hover lift is `shadow-press`: a hard 3px offset plus a 2px translate.
- Lay pages on a visible grid where it helps: PageGrid with `np-grid--rules` draws hairline column rules in `line`; align content to them.

## Layout

- Centre page content in `np-container`: max width `container` (1200px), side padding `gutter` (24px), `gutter-sm` (16px) below `bp-sm`.
- Stop reading text at `measure` (68ch) and leads under headings at `measure-short` (52ch). Components apply both; don't set `max-width` on text inline.
- Three breakpoints. Below `bp-lg` (1080px) the Docs layout hides its On this page column. Below `bp-md` (720px) Nav collapses to Menu, Split rows stack and Docs drops to one column. Below `bp-sm` (640px) display type drops one step, Feed rows and the Pager stack, and the gutter narrows. Check every page at 390px and 1280px.
- Layers: `z-menu` for menus, `z-dialog` for dialogs, `z-toast` for the toast stack, `z-tooltip` for tooltips. Nothing else sets a z-index.

## Docs pages

Build a docs page from one recipe, in this order:

1. `np-docs` with three children: `np-docs__side` (Sidebar), `np-docs__main`, `np-docs__toc` (On this page).
2. In main: Breadcrumb, then ArticleHeader, then Prose. Put Callouts and Tabs inside the Prose.
3. End main with a Rule and the Pager.

One page, one `aria-current` per list: the open page in the Sidebar, the visible heading in On this page.

## Slides

Decks use the same palette and faces at slide scale. Measured in the stress-test deck, 2026-10-13.

- Canvas 1920×1080, 128px margins, footer band at 64px from the bottom.
- Type: the `Slides` group in tokens: `slide-display` 200, `slide-statement` 120, `slide-quote` 88, `slide-title` 72, `slide-body` 32, `slide-label` 24. Nothing below 24px: `label` and `meta` both become `slide-label`.
- Hairlines double to 2px. 1px disappears on a projector.
- Slide tools take hex, not variables: use the values in `tokens.json` for the slide's theme.
- Rhythm: Paper for content, Deep for quotes and terminals, one `neptune` statement slide with `on-neptune` text near the end.
- Every content slide: eyebrow (`02 · Tools`), title at the top margin, one idea, footer stamp `NEPTUNE / 1.1 · 03`.
- Status in tables: the colour plus a word and a `●`.

## Ornament

Use typographic glyphs, not icons or emoji. In mono, `ink-muted`:

| Glyph | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `→` | Link and button suffix: "Read more →" |
| `›` | Prompt: inputs, breadcrumbs |
| `·` | Separator in metadata strings |
| `∴` | Section break centred in `np-rule` |
| `◆` | Bullet for featured items |
| `┌ ┐ └ ┘` | Corner marks framing a figure or hero image |
| `⌘K` | Search, always in `np-kbd` |
| `▾` | Open disclosure and select menus |
| `←` | Previous, in the Pager only |

## Imagery

- Prefer dithered or halftone treatments of classical subjects (sculpture, engravings, star charts) printed in `ink` on `paper`, or `neptune` on `paper` for one hero.
- Diagrams in hairlines, labelled in `meta`.
- No stock photos, no 3D blobs, no purple gradients.
- Frame every image in Figure (or the Card image slot). No bare images on paper.
- An image you don't have yet is an `np-slot` with a bracketed label (`[ Image · 16:9 ]`), never a grey box or a stock stand-in.

## Motion

- Fast and stepped: `duration-step` (80ms) with `easing-step` (`steps(2)`) for hover lift. Nothing eases in slowly.
- A blinking block cursor in terminals is the one ambient animation.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`: drop the cursor blink and the lift. `neptune.js` adds no motion of its own.

## Accessibility

- Measured 2026-10-13: every text pair meets 4.5:1 in both themes. Tightest: `alert` on `paper-sunk` 4.59:1 (Paper); `neptune` on `neptune-soft` 5.16:1 (Deep); `ink-muted` on `neptune-soft` 5.47:1 (Paper). `npm run contrast` measures these from `tokens.json`, and CI fails if any documented pair drops below its minimum.
- `line-strong` meets 3:1 on every paper surface, lowest 3.34:1 (Deep, `paper-raised`). `line` measures 1.25–1.47:1: decoration only, never the only edge of a control.
- Terminals and code blocks carry a `line` border: in Deep, `term-bg` almost matches `paper` and the block would lose its edge.
- On touch screens, buttons, nav links, toggles and inputs grow to a 44px target.
- Focus: 2px solid `focus`, 2px offset, on every interactive element. One rule in `bundle.css` sets it for everything inside `np-root`; don't override it.
- Status always carries a word, never colour alone.
- Every page starts with a SkipLink to `<main id="main">`. Text that only screen readers need goes in `np-visually-hidden`.
- Forced colours (Windows contrast themes): state carried by a fill or a blue glyph gets a system colour or an underline instead. Checkboxes, switches, the ThemeToggle, Tabs, the active nav link and search results all stay readable.
- Print is always Paper: nav, sidebars, search and toasts drop out, terminals print as outlined ink, and external links print their URL.
- Errors are announced, not just coloured: `aria-invalid="true"` on the control, `aria-describedby` pointing at the hint. Disabled controls say why in their hint.

## Logo

The mark is Neptune's trident (♆), square-stroked on a 24-unit grid in a `neptune` tile; the lockup adds the wordmark, "Neptune" in Newsreader 500 at -0.01em. Files, sizes, clear space and the favicon and social card are in Logo. Where the mark would be the only blue on a page that has spent its `neptune`, use the single-ink version.

## Versions

Neptune follows semantic versioning. The public surface is the token names, the `np-` classes and their documented markup.

Sites pin a release tag (`github:JosephSearle/neptune#v1.1.0`, see [Install](#install)) and upgrade by changing it. A tag never moves, so a site only changes when its tag does.

- Major (2.0): removing or renaming a token, class, component or modifier; changing what a token means; markup changes existing pages must make.
- Minor (1.2): new tokens, components, variants and states; visual refinements that existing markup picks up unchanged.
- Patch (1.1.1): bug fixes, docs, and value nudges that keep contrast and meaning.

Deprecation comes before removal, for at least one minor release:

1. Mark it in its README: `[ DEPRECATED · 1.x · use np-new ]`, and in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) under Deprecated.
2. Keep it working: an old class stays as an alias in `bundle.css`; an old token becomes an alias of the new one, its usage note starting "Deprecated:".
3. Remove it in the next major, listed under Removed with what replaces it.

A release updates the version stamps (README, Cover, Nav, Hero, Footer previews, `package.json`), moves the Unreleased entries in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) under the new number, and bumps `package.json`; on push, the release workflow tags `vX.Y.Z` and publishes the GitHub release from that section. That tag is what sites install.

## Changelog

Every release, newest first, is in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). The current release is 1.1.0.

## Maintainers

- Joseph Searle ([@JosephSearle](https://github.com/JosephSearle))

## Contributing

Neptune is a personal system, so it doesn't take pull requests for new direction. Bug reports and fixes are welcome. Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for how to report a bug, set up, and get a pull request merged.

Before you push, run the checks:

```bash
npm run check
npm run visual
npm run a11y
```

`npm run check` runs everything CI runs: tokens in sync, every documented colour pair at its WCAG minimum, `llms.txt` current, `neptune.js` parses, a stylelint pass on `components/` that rejects raw colours (hex, `rgb()`, named colours) and any `z-index` that isn't a `z-` token, and `scripts/check-pack.mjs`, which fails if a git install would miss a site file, ship anything outside `files` in `package.json`, or run an install script. A new colour goes into `tokens.json` (and `tokens/primitives.json`) first.

Visual regression: `tests/visual.spec.js` screenshots every component preview in Paper and Deep, with the brand fonts served locally, and CI compares them with `tests/__screenshots__` on every push. After an intended visual change, run the **visual** workflow by hand with *update* ticked; it rewrites the baselines in the same container CI uses and commits them.

Accessibility: `tests/a11y.spec.js` runs axe-core on every component preview in Paper and Deep, in the same container, and the **a11y** workflow fails on any serious or critical violation. Fix the markup, the README or the CSS; don't add an ignore unless the violation is preview-only scaffolding, and say why next to it.

Follow [Versions](#versions) for anything that changes a token, class or component.

# ArticleHeader

The top of a note or playbook: a kind-and-date stamp, the title, a lead, then byline and tags, closed by a hairline.

- Markup: `<header class="np-article-head">` holding `p.np-article-head__stamp` (`Playbook · 2026-10-08 · 8 min`), `h1.np-article-head__title`, `p.np-article-head__lead`, and `div.np-article-head__foot` with `p.np-article-head__byline` and a row of tags.
- In the DocsLayout, a Breadcrumb goes above it.
- Byline: `By <strong>Joseph Searle</strong> · Updated 2026-10-12`. Show "Updated" only when the page changed after publishing.
- Read time is true or absent: compute it from the word count (about 230 words a minute) or leave it out.
- One to three tags, from the same fixed set as the Feed.
- The title wraps at 20 characters wide and drops to `heading` size below `bp-sm`.

## Anatomy

```text
┌ header.np-article-head ─────────────────────────┐
│ __stamp         Playbook · 2026-10-08 · 8 min   │
│ __title         h1, serif display               │
│ __lead          one sentence, ink-muted         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ __foot          __byline · row of np-tag        │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Source: components/ArticleHeader/README.md · Preview: components/ArticleHeader/preview.html

---

# Breadcrumb

The path from the docs root to the current page, in mono with › separators.

- Markup: `<nav class="np-crumbs" aria-label="Breadcrumb">` holding an `ol` of `li`. Every item but the last is a link; the last is a `span` with `aria-current="page"`.
- Sits above the page title, `space-4` above it.
- Consumer provides: the section names as they appear in the Sidebar, and the page title (shortened to a few words if long).
- Two to four levels. Skip it on top-level pages.
- Don't: link the current page, or use it as the only navigation.

## Keyboard

- Tab walks the linked levels; the current page isn't a link and isn't a tab stop.

Source: components/Breadcrumb/README.md · Preview: components/Breadcrumb/preview.html

---

# Button

A square, mono-labelled action that lifts on hover with `shadow-press`.

- Markup: `<button class="np-btn">` or `<a class="np-btn">`. Add `np-btn--primary` or `np-btn--ghost`.
- Consumer provides: the label (2–4 words, imperative), and an optional `→` suffix for navigation.
- One `np-btn--primary` per view. Secondary is the default.
- Ghost is for low-weight links in a row of actions.
- Danger (`np-btn--danger`) fills `alert` with `on-alert` text. Use it only as the confirm button of a destructive Dialog; the button that opens that Dialog is a normal secondary.
- States: hover lifts, `:active` presses flat, focus shows the ring. Disabled: `disabled` on a `<button>`; on an `<a>`, drop the `href` and add `aria-disabled="true"`. Busy: `aria-busy="true"` while the action runs; keep the label, a blinking block follows it, and set `disabled` too so it can't fire twice.
- Say why a control is disabled, in a hint or nearby text. A dead button with no reason is a dead end.
- Do: "Read the playbook →", "View source", "Copy".
- Don't: sentence-case labels, icons without text, two primaries side by side.

## Keyboard

- Tab focuses; Enter activates; Space activates a `<button>` (not a link).
- A disabled `<button>` leaves the tab order; an `aria-disabled` link stays in it, so it can still explain itself.

Source: components/Button/README.md · Preview: components/Button/preview.html

---

# Callout

A boxed aside with a bracketed mono label: note, tip or warning.

- Markup: `<aside class="np-callout" role="note">` holding `div.np-callout__label` (`[ Note ]`) and `div.np-callout__body` with paragraphs, lists or code. Add `np-callout--tip` or `np-callout--warn`.
- Note: neutral, for context. Tip: `neptune`, for a shortcut or a better way. Warning: `alert`, for something that breaks or costs money.
- Write the label as a word in brackets. The colour never carries the meaning alone.
- Consumer provides: the kind, and one to three sentences. A callout longer than a paragraph is a section.
- Inside Prose it takes `space-8` above and below.
- Don't: stack two callouts, put a callout in a card, or add a coloured left edge.

## Anatomy

```text
┌ aside.np-callout ─────────────────────────────────┐
│ __label         [ Tip ], mono, coloured by kind   │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ __body          1–3 sentences, lists or code      │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Keyboard

- Not interactive. Links inside it are ordinary tab stops.

Source: components/Callout/README.md · Preview: components/Callout/preview.html

---

# Card

A square, hairline-bordered panel with a mono index bar, serif title and a metadata footer.

- Markup: `<a class="np-card">` (linked, lifts on hover) or `<div class="np-card">` (static). Parts: `np-card__bar`, `np-card__body`, `np-card__title`, `np-card__text`, `np-card__foot`.
- Consumer provides: index and category (`01 / Playbook`), title, one-sentence summary, ISO date, and a read time or action in the footer.
- Lay cards in a grid with `space-8` gaps. Indexes count up across the grid.
- Optional: one tag or a bracketed status (`[ Draft ]`) on the right of the bar.
- Optional image: `img.np-card__media` (with `alt`) between the bar and the body. 16:9 by default; add `np-ratio-square`, `np-ratio-portrait` or `np-ratio-wide` to change it. No image yet: `div.np-card__media.np-slot` with a `<span>` label (`[ IMAGE · 16:9 ]`).
- In a grid, give every card an image or none. Mixed rows break the baseline.
- Don't: add images inside the bar, colour the border, round the corners, add a coloured left edge.

## Anatomy

```text
┌ a.np-card ────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ __bar           01 / Playbook        [ tag ]      │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ __media         optional image or np-slot, 16:9   │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ __body          __title, then __text              │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ __foot          2026-10-08          8 min →       │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Keyboard

- A linked card is one tab stop: the whole card is the `<a>`. Don't nest other links or buttons inside it.

Source: components/Card/README.md · Preview: components/Card/preview.html

---

# Chart

The frame around a data plot: mono eyebrow, serif title, legend, an SVG plot with a hover readout, a source line, and the numbers as a table.

- Markup: `<figure class="np-chart">` holding `p.np-chart__eyebrow`, `h3.np-chart__title`, `ul.np-chart__legend` of `li.np-chart__key` (each sets `--key: var(--viz-N)`), `div.np-chart__plot` with the `<svg>` and a `div.np-chart__tip` (`hidden` until hover), `figcaption.np-chart__caption` (`Source: evals, 2026-10-07`), then `details.np-chart__data` with a Table.
- Draw the plot yourself (inline SVG, D3, Observable Plot); this component styles the frame and the SVG classes: `.grid`, `.axis`, `.tick text`, `.label`, `.direct`, `.hover-line`.

## Colour, by the job it does

- Identity (which series): `viz-1` to `viz-6`, assigned in order and never cycled. Colour follows the entity: a filter that drops a series doesn't repaint the rest. A seventh series folds into Other (`viz-other`).
- Scatter, bubble, maps and small multiples: at most three series (`viz-1` to `viz-3`), the only three that stay apart when any two can touch.
- Magnitude: `viz-seq-1` (least) to `viz-seq-7`, one hue. Deep flips the ramp so low values recede into the ground; use the tokens and it happens for you. For ordered buckets (tiers, funnel steps), start at `viz-seq-4` on Paper so every step clears 2:1.
- Polarity: `viz-div-neg-3…1`, `viz-div-mid`, `viz-div-pos-1…3`: gold below zero, blue above, neutral at zero. The weakest steps sit near the ground on purpose; label values.
- State: when a series means good or bad, it wears `ok` or `alert` with a word, never a `viz-` slot.
- Measured 2026-10-13 on `paper` and Deep `paper`: every series at least 3:1, adjacent series at least 16.5 apart under protan/deutan simulation (target 8) and 21 apart for full-colour vision (floor 15); the first three at least 11.6 apart as any pair.

## Marks

- Lines 2px, square caps. Bars square, with a 2px `paper` gap between neighbours and stacked segments. Points at least 8px.
- Text wears ink tokens, never the series colour. Direct-label up to four series at the line end (`.direct`); always show the legend for two or more. One series: no legend, the title names it.
- One y-axis. Two measures on different scales are two charts.
- Gridlines in `viz-grid`, baseline in `viz-axis`. No chart junk: no 3D, no gradients, no shadows.

## Interaction and access

- Hover or focus shows the readout in `np-chart__tip`: a crosshair on line charts, per-mark on bars. Hit areas larger than the mark.
- Keyboard: the plot takes focus (`tabindex="0"`); Left and Right step through x values and update the readout, Esc hides it.
- The `details` table holds every number in the chart. A chart without it fails for screen readers, print and forced colours.
- Give the `<svg>` `role="img"` and an `aria-label` that states the takeaway, not "a chart".

- Don't: use a pie with more than three slices, label every point, or use colour as the only key.

## Anatomy

```text
┌ figure.np-chart ──────────────────────────────────┐
│ __eyebrow       Fig. 03 · Evals                   │
│ __title         serif, the takeaway               │
│ __legend        ■ series  ■ series  ■ series      │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ __plot          svg role=img + __tip readout      │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ __caption       Source: …, date                   │
│ __data          details › Table of every number   │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Source: components/Chart/README.md · Preview: components/Chart/preview.html

---

# Checkbox

Checkboxes and radio buttons: a square (round for radio) that fills with a `neptune` mark when checked.

- Markup: `<label class="np-check"><input type="checkbox"> Label</label>`. Same for `type="radio"`.
- Group related options in `fieldset.np-fieldset` with a `legend` styled `np-field__label`.
- Checkbox for independent options; radio for one of several. Two to six radios; more is a Select.
- Labels are serif, sentence case, and say what happens when checked.
- Disabled: add `disabled` to the input; the label turns `ink-muted`.
- Don't: use a checkbox for an action that applies at once. Use a Switch.

## Keyboard

- Tab moves between checkboxes; Space toggles.
- Radios are one tab stop per group: Tab enters, Up/Down or Left/Right move and select.

Source: components/Checkbox/README.md · Preview: components/Checkbox/preview.html

# CodeCopy

A dark code block with a language label and a Copy button, plus a light inline code style.

- Markup: `<div class="np-code">` with `np-code__head` (language + `button.np-code__copy`) and `<pre><code>`. Inside, `.p` for prompts and `.c` for commands. Inline: `<code class="np-code-inline">`.
- Consumer provides: the language label and the code.
- Behaviour comes from `neptune.js`: Copy copies the code with prompts (`$ `) stripped, then reads "Copied" for 1.5s with `data-copied` set. No toast.
- Use Terminal for transcripts with output; use CodeCopy for things people paste.

## Anatomy

```text
┌ div.np-code ─────────────────────────────────────┐
│ __head          bash                  [ Copy ]   │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ pre > code      .p prompt  .c command            │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Keyboard

- Tab reaches Copy; Enter or Space copies. The label change to "Copied" is the confirmation; nothing moves focus.

Source: components/CodeCopy/README.md · Preview: components/CodeCopy/preview.html

# Dialog

A native modal for confirmations and short tasks: bracketed label, serif title, body, and actions on a sunk footer.

- Markup: `<dialog class="np-dialog" aria-labelledby="…" aria-describedby="…">` holding `form.np-dialog__box` with `method="dialog"`: `p.np-dialog__label` (`[ Confirm ]`), `h2.np-dialog__title`, `div.np-dialog__body`, `div.np-dialog__foot`.
- Open with `showModal()`: give the trigger `data-np-open="<dialog id>"` and `neptune.js` does it. The browser gives the focus trap, Esc and the backdrop. On close, focus returns to the button that opened it; set it yourself if that button is gone.
- Buttons in the foot carry `value`; read `dialog.returnValue` on `close`. Esc returns an empty value: treat it as Cancel.
- Order: Cancel, then the action, right-aligned. On phones they stack, action on top.
- Consumer provides: a title that asks the question ("Delete mcp-gateway?"), one or two sentences on what happens, and a button that names the action ("Delete project", never "OK" or "Yes").

## Destructive actions

- Add `np-dialog--danger`: the label turns `alert` and reads `[ Delete ]` or `[ Irreversible ]`.
- The confirm button is `np-btn--danger`, the only place it appears. Put `autofocus` on Cancel, so Enter can't destroy anything by accident.
- Say what is lost, with numbers where you have them: "its 14 runs and 3 API keys".
- Irreversible and large: add an Input asking for the name, and keep the action `disabled` until it matches. Put `data-np-confirm="<name>"` on the input and `neptune.js` enables the `np-btn--danger` button when the trimmed text matches.

- Don't: open a dialog on page load, stack two dialogs, or use one for a message that needs no decision (use a Toast).

## Anatomy

```text
┌ dialog.np-dialog ──────────────────────────────┐
│ __label         [ Confirm ]                    │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ __title         the question                   │
│ __body          what happens; optional field   │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ __foot          Cancel   Action                │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Keyboard

- Tab cycles inside the dialog only; Esc cancels; Enter on a focused button presses it.
- Focus starts on Cancel in a danger dialog, on the first field otherwise.

Source: components/Dialog/README.md · Preview: components/Dialog/preview.html

---

# DocsLayout

The three-column docs page: Sidebar, content, On this page.

- Markup: `div.np-docs` inside `<main id="main" tabindex="-1" class="np-container">`, after a SkipLink and the Nav, holding `aside.np-docs__side` (Sidebar), `article.np-docs__main` and `aside.np-docs__toc` (Toc), in that order.
- Columns: 240px · fluid · 200px. Below `bp-lg` (1080px) the Toc column hides. Below `bp-md` (720px) one column, Sidebar first.
- Main runs: Breadcrumb, `display` title, Prose (with Callouts and Tabs), Rule, Pager. The README's Docs pages section has the full recipe.
- The side columns are sticky at `space-8` from the top.
- Consumer provides: the three regions. Nothing else goes in the grid.

## Anatomy

```text
┌ main > div.np-docs ─────────────────────────────────┐
│ __side          Sidebar, 240px, sticky              │
│ __main          Breadcrumb · ArticleHeader ·        │
│                 Prose · Rule · Pager                │
│ __toc           Toc, 200px, sticky; hidden < 1080   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Source: components/DocsLayout/README.md · Preview: components/DocsLayout/preview.html

# EmptyState

What shows when a list, a search or a page has nothing in it: a mono frame glyph, what is empty, what to do, and at most one action.

- Markup: `div.np-empty` holding `pre.np-empty__art` (`aria-hidden="true"`), `p.np-empty__title`, `p.np-empty__text`, and an optional `div.np-row` with one button.
- Title says what is empty, specifically: `No notes match "gateway".` Not "Nothing here".
- Text says what to do next: `Check the spelling, or search playbooks instead.`
- Art: a small box drawn in box glyphs with `∴` inside. Same art everywhere.
- Inside the SearchDialog it drops its border and background.
- Don't: add an illustration, a joke, or more than one action.

## Anatomy

```text
┌ div.np-empty ───────────────────────────────────────┐
│ __art           ┌─┐ box glyph with ∴, aria-hidden   │
│ __title         what is empty, specifically         │
│ __text          what to do next                     │
│ np-row          at most one button                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Source: components/EmptyState/README.md · Preview: components/EmptyState/preview.html

# Feed

A dated list of entries, one row each: ISO date, serif title, tag.

- Markup: `ol.np-feed` holding `li.np-feed__item`, each with `a.np-feed__link` containing `time.np-feed__date` (with `datetime`), `span.np-feed__title` and one `np-tag`.
- Newest first. Dates in ISO (`2026-10-08`). One tag per row, from a short fixed set (`Playbook`, `Research`, `Notes`).
- The whole row is the link; the title turns `neptune` and underlines on hover.
- Below 640px the date and tag share the first line and the title takes the second.
- Consumer provides: date, title in sentence case, tag, and the link.
- Open it with a SectionHead. Close long feeds with a ghost button (`All notes →`), not pagination.
- Don't: add summaries or thumbnails to rows. Use Card for that.

## Anatomy

```text
┌ ol.np-feed › li.np-feed__item › a.np-feed__link ────┐
│ __date          time, ISO                           │
│ __title         serif, sentence case                │
│ np-tag          one, from a fixed set               │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Keyboard

- One tab stop per row: the whole row is the link.

Source: components/Feed/README.md · Preview: components/Feed/preview.html

# Figure

A framed image with ┌ ┘ corner marks and a numbered `FIG.` caption.

- Markup: `<figure class="np-figure">` holding `div.np-figure__frame` with `img.np-figure__media` inside, then `figcaption.np-figure__caption` with `span.np-figure__num` (`Fig. 01`) and the caption text.
- No image yet: put `div.np-figure__media.np-slot` with a `<span>` label (`[ Image · 16:9 ]`) in the frame instead of the `img`.
- Ratio: 16:9 by default. Add `np-ratio-square`, `np-ratio-portrait` or `np-ratio-wide` to the `figure`.
- Consumer provides: the image with real `alt` text, a figure number counting up through the page, and a one-line caption in sentence case.
- Images follow the brand's imagery rules: dithered or halftone classical subjects, diagrams in hairlines. No stock photos.
- Don't: round the frame, add a shadow, set the caption in italic, or drop the number.

## Anatomy

```text
┌ figure.np-figure ──────────────────────────┐
│ __frame         ┌ corner marks ┘           │
│   __media       img, or np-slot            │
├────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ __caption       __num Fig. 01 · one line   │
└────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Source: components/Figure/README.md · Preview: components/Figure/preview.html

# Footer

The page closer on `paper-sunk`: link columns with mono headings, a metadata line, and an oversized serif wordmark cropped by the page edge.

- Markup: `<footer class="np-footer">` with `np-footer__cols` (each `np-footer__col` an `h4` + `ul`), `np-footer__meta`, and `p.np-footer__giant` marked `aria-hidden`.
- Consumer provides: 2–4 columns of 3–5 links, the version stamp, and the copyright line.
- The giant wordmark is decorative and sits flush with the bottom edge, cropped at the descenders. It stays type: the mark is for small sizes and the Nav.
- One footer per page.

## Anatomy

```text
┌ footer.np-footer ────────────────────────────────┐
│ __cols          2–4 × __col: h4 + ul of links    │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ __meta          stamp · © · built with           │
│ __giant         wordmark, aria-hidden, cropped   │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Keyboard

- Tab walks the columns left to right, top to bottom. The giant wordmark is hidden from assistive tech and never focused.

Source: components/Footer/README.md · Preview: components/Footer/preview.html

# Hero

The page opener: a mono stamp, a `display-xl` serif headline, a lead, actions and an optional stats strip, framed by ┌ ┘ corner marks.

- Markup: `<section class="np-hero">` with `np-hero__eyebrow`, `h1.np-hero__title`, `p.np-hero__lead`, an `np-row` of buttons, and optional `dl.np-hero__stats`.
- Consumer provides: a stamp (`NEPTUNE / 0.1 · LDN · TOPIC`), a headline under 10 words, a one-sentence lead, one primary and one secondary action.
- Put one word of the headline in `<em>` to set it in italic `neptune`. Once only.
- Stats must be real and countable. No stats beats fake stats.
- One hero per page. Below 640px the headline drops to `display` size.

## Anatomy

```text
┌ section.np-hero ─────────────────────────────┐
│ __eyebrow       mono stamp                   │
│ __title         h1, display-xl, one <em>     │
│ __lead          ≤ 52ch                       │
│ np-row          primary + secondary button   │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ __stats         optional dl of dt/dd         │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Source: components/Hero/README.md · Preview: components/Hero/preview.html

# Input

A mono text field with a `›` prompt, an uppercase label and a hint line.

- Markup: `<label class="np-field">` holding `np-field__label`, `<span class="np-input"><input></span>` and `np-field__hint`. Add `np-field--error` for errors.
- Consumer provides: label (1–2 words), placeholder showing the expected format, and a hint.
- Error hints say what went wrong, then what to do: "Invalid name: spaces not allowed. Use kebab-case."
- Errors: set `aria-invalid="true"` on the control and point `aria-describedby` at the hint's `id`, so the error is announced. The border, prompt and hint turn `alert`. `np-field--error` on the field still works for the look, but always add `aria-invalid` too.
- Disabled: `disabled` on the control. The box sinks to `paper-sunk` and the text mutes. Say why in the hint.
- Read-only: `readonly` on the input. It sits on `paper-sunk`, stays focusable and copyable. Use it for values a reader can see but not change, like an ID.
- The focus ring is on the wrapper (`:focus-within`), so the prompt glyph stays inside it.

## Anatomy

```text
┌ label.np-field ────────────────────────────────────┐
│ __label         EMAIL, mono uppercase              │
│ np-input        › prompt + input                   │
│ __hint          format, or the error and its fix   │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Keyboard

- Tab focuses the field; the ring is on the whole box.
- Hint and error text are reached by screen readers through `aria-describedby`, not by tabbing.

Source: components/Input/README.md · Preview: components/Input/preview.html

---

# Kbd

A physical-looking key for shortcuts, with a 2px bottom edge.

- Markup: `<kbd class="np-kbd">K</kbd>`. One key per element; chords are adjacent keys separated by a space.
- Consumer provides: the key name. Use symbols for modifiers: ⌘ ⇧ ⌥ ⌃.
- Show the shortcut beside the action it triggers, e.g. in the nav search button.

Source: components/Kbd/README.md · Preview: components/Kbd/preview.html

# Logo

The mark is Neptune's trident (♆, the planet's astronomical sign) drawn on a 24-unit grid with 2-unit square strokes, in a `neptune` square. The lockup sets it beside the "Neptune" wordmark in Newsreader 500, outlined.

- Files in `brand/`: `neptune-mark.svg` and `neptune-mark-deep.svg` (the tile), `neptune-mark-ink.svg` (single ink, no tile), `neptune-lockup.svg` and `neptune-lockup-deep.svg`, the favicon set (`favicon.svg`, `favicon.ico`, `apple-touch-icon.png`, `icon-192.png`, `icon-512.png`) and the social card (`og-template.html`, `og-default.png`). `scripts/build-brand.py` makes them all from `tokens.json`; don't edit them by hand.
- Paper pages use the Paper files, Deep pages the Deep ones. `favicon.svg` switches with the system theme by itself.
- Single ink (`neptune-mark-ink.svg`, in `ink`) is for print, embossing, one-colour merch, and anywhere the blue tile would be the only colour on a page that already spends its `neptune`.
- Clear space: half the tile on every side. Nothing else enters it, including other marks and the page edge.
- Minimum size: 16px for the mark, 24px tile height for the lockup. Below that, set the wordmark in type.
- In the Nav, the mark (20px) may sit before the wordmark; the text wordmark stays, so the name is still text.

## Head tags

```html
<link rel="icon" href="/favicon.ico" sizes="48x48">
<link rel="icon" href="/favicon.svg" type="image/svg+xml">
<link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="/apple-touch-icon.png">
<meta property="og:image" content="https://…/og-default.png">
```

## Social card

`brand/og-template.html` is a 1200×630 card: stamp, serif title, kind and date, the trident on a `neptune` slab. Open it with `?kind=Playbook&title=MCP%20servers%20in%20production&date=2026-10-08` and screenshot it at 1200×630 for each page; `og-default.png` is the fallback.

- Don't: recolour the mark (other than single ink), round the tile, add a shadow or gradient, rotate it, outline it, set the wordmark in another face, or stretch either.

Source: components/Logo/README.md · Preview: components/Logo/preview.html

# Nav

The top bar: serif wordmark with a mono version stamp, uppercase mono links and a ⌘K search.

- Markup: `<nav class="np-nav">` with `np-nav__brand` (`np-nav__mark` + `np-meta`), `ul.np-nav__links`, and `div.np-nav__actions` holding `button.np-nav__search` (label in `span.np-search-text`), an optional ThemeToggle, and `details.np-nav__menu`.
- Consumer provides: 3–5 links, the current page marked `aria-current="page"`, and a version stamp. Repeat the links inside `details.np-nav__menu > ul`.
- The active link turns `neptune`. Nothing else in the bar is blue.
- Below 720px the CSS hides `np-nav__links` and the search label, and shows the "Menu" disclosure. No JavaScript needed; `<details>` handles open, close and keyboard.

## Anatomy

```text
┌ nav.np-nav ───────────────────────────────────────┐
│ __brand         __mark wordmark + np-meta stamp   │
│ __links         3–5 links, one aria-current       │
│ __actions       __search ⌘K · ThemeToggle ·       │
│                 __menu (details, < 720px)         │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Keyboard

- Tab order: wordmark, links, search, theme, menu.
- ⌘K / Ctrl+K opens SearchDialog from anywhere on the page.
- Below 720px the Menu is a `<details>`: Enter or Space opens it, Tab walks its links.

Source: components/Nav/README.md · Preview: components/Nav/preview.html

# PageGrid

A 12-column grid (4 below `bp-md`) with an optional hairline rule at every column edge: the visible grid the brand book asks for.

- Markup: `div.np-grid` inside `np-container`. Children take `np-span-3`, `-4`, `-6`, `-8`, `-9` or `-12`. Add `np-grid--rules` to draw the column rules in `line`.
- Column gap is `gutter`; row gap is `space-8`. Below `bp-md` every child spans the full width and the rules redraw for 4 columns.
- Use the rules on index pages, landing sections and anything laid out as a sheet. Leave them off behind long reading text.
- Content with its own surface (Card, Figure) sits over the rules; bare text sits between them.
- Common splits: 8 + 4 (content and aside), 4 + 4 + 4 (cards), 3 + 9 (label and body).
- Don't: nest grids, or set column widths inline.

Source: components/PageGrid/README.md · Preview: components/PageGrid/preview.html

---

# Pager

Previous and next links at the foot of a docs page.

- Markup: `<nav class="np-pager" aria-label="Pages">` with up to two `a.np-pager__link`, the second with `np-pager__link--next`. Each holds `span.np-pager__dir` (`← Previous`, `Next →`) and `span.np-pager__title`.
- First page: next only; it stays in the right column. Last page: previous only.
- Below 640px the links stack, previous first.
- Consumer provides: the neighbouring pages in Sidebar order, with their real titles.
- Don't: number pages, or use it for anything but reading order.

## Anatomy

```text
┌ nav.np-pager ────────────────────────────────┐
│ __link          __dir ← Previous · __title   │
│ __link--next    __dir Next → · __title       │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Keyboard

- Two tab stops, previous then next. Each link's text names the page it goes to.

Source: components/Pager/README.md · Preview: components/Pager/preview.html

---

# Prose

A wrapper that applies Neptune's type to plain article HTML: headings, paragraphs, lists, links, quotes and inline code.

- Markup: `<article class="np-prose">` around rendered Markdown or MDX.
- Consumer provides: the content. No classes needed inside.
- Max width is 68ch. `h2` maps to `heading`, `h3` to `title`, `blockquote` to `quote`.
- Put code blocks in CodeCopy, not bare `<pre>`.

Source: components/Prose/README.md · Preview: components/Prose/preview.html

---

# Rule

A hairline section break with a centred glyph or eyebrow label.

- Markup: `<div class="np-rule">∴</div>`, or put a short mono label inside: `02 · Research`.
- Use `∴` between sections of long-form text; use an indexed label to open a page section.
- Don't stack two rules, or use one directly under a heading.

Source: components/Rule/README.md · Preview: components/Rule/preview.html

---

# SearchDialog

The ⌘K search: a native modal dialog with a prompt input, grouped results and key hints.

- Markup: `<dialog class="np-search" aria-label="Search">` holding `form.np-search__box` (an `np-input` with `type="search"` and an `Esc` Kbd), `div.np-search__results` and `div.np-search__foot` with key hints.
- Results are a listbox, with the input as its combobox. The input takes `role="combobox"`, `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` pointing at the results' `id`, and `aria-activedescendant` naming the selected result. `div.np-search__results` takes `role="listbox"` and an `aria-label`. Per group: `div[role="group"]` labelled by its `p.np-search__group`, holding `ul.np-search__list[role="none"]` of `li[role="none"]` > `a.np-search__item[role="option"]`, each with an `id`, `tabindex="-1"` and `aria-selected`.
- `neptune.js` opens it with `showModal()` from the Nav search button (`np-nav__search`) and from ⌘K / Ctrl+K, and focuses the input. One per page. The browser handles Esc, the focus trap and the backdrop.
- Keyboard: focus stays in the input. Up and Down move `aria-selected` and `aria-activedescendant` through results; Enter opens the selected one. `neptune.js` handles all three.
- Each result: the title, with the matched words in `<mark>`, and its section in `np-meta` on the right.
- No results: put an EmptyState in the results area.
- Results read from a prebuilt index; nothing loads until the dialog opens.

## Anatomy

```text
┌ dialog.np-search ──────────────────────────────┐
│ __box           np-input type=search · Esc     │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ __results       __group + ul of __item         │
│                 title with <mark> · np-meta    │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ __foot          ↑↓ move · ↵ open · esc close   │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Source: components/SearchDialog/README.md · Preview: components/SearchDialog/preview.html

---

# SectionHead

The opener for a page section: an optional indexed rule, a serif heading, an optional lead and an optional action on the right.

- Markup: `<header class="np-section-head">` with an optional `div.np-rule`, then `div.np-section-head__row` holding `h2.np-section-head__title` and an optional ghost button, then an optional `p.np-section-head__lead`. Add `np-section-head--sm` for sub-sections.
- Consumer provides: the index and name for the rule (`01 · Notes`), the heading in sentence case, and at most one action.
- Index sections in page order. The heading drops to `heading` size below 640px.
- Use this instead of styling `h2` inline.

## Anatomy

```text
┌ header.np-section-head ───────────────────────────┐
│ np-rule         optional 02 · Research            │
│ __row           __title · optional ghost button   │
│ __lead          optional, ≤ 52ch                  │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Source: components/SectionHead/README.md · Preview: components/SectionHead/preview.html

---

# Select

A native select in the Input box, mono text, ▾ on the right.

- Markup: inside `label.np-field`: `span.np-field__label`, then `<span class="np-select"><select>…</select></span>`, then an optional `span.np-field__hint`.
- Use for one of seven or more options. Fewer: radio buttons, so every option shows.
- Keep the native `select`: it brings the phone picker and keyboard support for free.
- Errors: set `aria-invalid="true"` on the control and point `aria-describedby` at the hint's `id`, so the error is announced. The border, prompt and hint turn `alert`. `np-field--error` on the field still works for the look, but always add `aria-invalid` too.
- Disabled: `disabled` on the control. The box sinks to `paper-sunk` and the text mutes. Say why in the hint.
- Consumer provides: options in a sensible order (most used first, or alphabetical), and a default.

## Keyboard

- Tab focuses; Space or Alt+Down opens the native list; Up and Down change the value; type to jump.

Source: components/Select/README.md · Preview: components/Select/preview.html

---

# Sidebar

Grouped navigation for a docs site, inside a disclosure that ships open.

- Markup: `<details class="np-sidebar" open>` with a `summary` (`Contents`), then one `div.np-sidebar__group` per section: `p.np-sidebar__heading` (`01 · MCP`) and a `ul` of links. The open page's link gets `aria-current="page"`.
- Group headings are indexed in order. Page links are sentence case, as their titles.
- Lives in `np-docs__side`, sticky. Below `bp-md` it stacks above the page; a reader closes it with one tap.
- Consumer provides: sections in reading order, pages in each, and the current page.
- Keep groups to about eight pages. More: split the group.
- Don't: nest beyond one level, or add icons.

## Anatomy

```text
┌ details.np-sidebar[open] ───────────────────────┐
│ summary         Contents                        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ __group         __heading 01 · MCP              │
│                 ul of links, one aria-current   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ __group         …                               │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Keyboard

- Tab walks the links in reading order; the `summary` toggles the list with Enter or Space.

Source: components/Sidebar/README.md · Preview: components/Sidebar/preview.html

---

# SkipLink

A "Skip to content" link, hidden until a keyboard user tabs to it, so they can jump past the Nav and Sidebar.

- Markup: `<a class="np-skip" href="#main">Skip to content</a>` as the first child of `<body>`. The target is `<main id="main" tabindex="-1">`, wrapping the page content after the Nav.
- On focus it appears top left as a `neptune` block with `on-neptune` mono text.
- Every page gets one, including pages without a Sidebar: the Nav alone is several tab stops.
- `tabindex="-1"` lets the browser move focus into `main`; Neptune hides the outline there because nothing visible is focused.

## Visually hidden

`np-visually-hidden` keeps text in the accessibility tree but off the screen: a label for an icon-only control, a "(opens in a new tab)" note, a table caption that sighted readers get from context. It shows again if the element takes focus.

Source: components/SkipLink/README.md · Preview: components/SkipLink/preview.html

---

# Split

A row of text beside a figure, alternating sides down the page.

- Markup: `div.np-splits` holding one `section.np-split` per row. Each row holds `div.np-split__text` (an `np-meta` eyebrow, `h3.np-split__title`, `p.np-split__lead`, an optional button) and an `np-figure`.
- Inside `np-splits`, even rows put the text on the right automatically. For a single row, add `np-split--reverse` to flip it.
- Keep text first in the markup. Below 720px rows stack, text above the figure.
- Consumer provides: an eyebrow (`02 · Retrieval`), a title in sentence case, a lead of one or two sentences, and the figure.
- Use for walk-throughs and feature tours. Two to four rows; more becomes a list, so use Feed.
- Don't: put two figures in a row, or a card in place of the figure.

## Anatomy

```text
┌ div.np-splits › section.np-split ────────────────┐
│ __text          np-meta · __title · __lead ·     │
│                 optional button                  │
│ np-figure       alternates sides; stacks < 720   │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Source: components/Split/README.md · Preview: components/Split/preview.html

---

# Switch

An on/off control for a setting that applies at once. Square track, square thumb; on fills `neptune`.

- Markup: `<label class="np-switch"><input type="checkbox" role="switch"> Label</label>`.
- The label names the setting, not the state: "Compact tables", not "Turn on compact tables".
- Use for settings that take effect immediately. For choices submitted with a form, use a Checkbox.
- Disabled: add `disabled` to the input.
- Don't: pair a switch with a Save button.

## Keyboard

- Tab focuses; Space toggles, and the change applies at once. Screen readers announce on/off via `role="switch"`.

Source: components/Switch/README.md · Preview: components/Switch/preview.html

---

# Table

A data table with mono uppercase headers on `paper-sunk`, serif cells, hairline rows and right-aligned tabular numbers.

- Markup: `<div class="np-table-wrap"><table class="np-table">`. Add `class="num"` to numeric headers and cells, `class="idx"` to an index column.
- Consumer provides: column headers (1–2 words), rows, and units in the cell ("420 ms"), not the header.
- Use Tag for status columns, with a word. Rows highlight `neptune-soft` on hover.
- The wrapper scrolls horizontally on phones; don't hide columns.
- Optional `<caption>` for a mono source line: "Source: evals, 2026-10-07".

## Anatomy

```text
┌ div.np-table-wrap › table.np-table ───────────────┐
│ caption         optional source line              │
│ thead th        mono uppercase on paper-sunk      │
│ tbody td        serif; .num right-aligned, .idx   │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Source: components/Table/README.md · Preview: components/Table/preview.html

# Tabs

Mono tabs over panels, for alternatives a reader picks one of: package managers, languages, operating systems.

- Markup: `div.np-tabs` holding `div.np-tabs__list` with `role="tablist"` and an `aria-label`, then one `div.np-tabs__panel` per tab with `role="tabpanel"`. Tabs are `button.np-tabs__tab` with `role="tab"`, `aria-selected`, `aria-controls` and an `id`; panels carry `aria-labelledby` and `hidden` when not shown.
- Behaviour comes from `neptune.js`: click selects, and only the selected tab is in the tab order (`tabindex="-1"` on the rest). Call `Neptune.init(el)` after adding tabs to a live page.
- The selected tab carries a 2px `neptune` underline. That is the view's one blue.
- Consumer provides: two to five short labels and a panel each, usually a CodeCopy.
- Don't: use tabs for content a reader needs to compare. Show it side by side.

## Anatomy

```text
┌ div.np-tabs ────────────────────────────────┐
│ __list          role=tablist: __tab × 2–5   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ __panel         role=tabpanel, one shown    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Keyboard

- Tab moves into the tab list onto the selected tab, then out to its panel.
- Left and Right move to the previous or next tab and select it, wrapping at the ends.
- Home and End move to the first and last tab and select it.

Source: components/Tabs/README.md · Preview: components/Tabs/preview.html

---

# Tag

A square mono label for categories, licences and status.

- Markup: `<span class="np-tag">`. Variants: `np-tag--accent`, `np-tag--ok`, `np-tag--alert`.
- Consumer provides: 1–3 words. Separate parts with ` · `.
- Status tags (`ok`, `alert`) include `<span class="np-dot">` and a word. Never colour alone.
- One accent tag per card at most.
- Don't: round the corners, use emoji, use tags as buttons.

Source: components/Tag/README.md · Preview: components/Tag/preview.html

---

# Terminal

A dark code and command block with a mono title bar; stays dark in both themes.

- Markup: `<div class="np-term">` with `np-term__bar` and `<pre class="np-term__body">`. Inside the body: `.p` for prompts and comments, `.c` for commands, `.cur` for the block cursor.
- Consumer provides: a bar label (`[ TUI ] ~/path`), real commands and real output.
- Show commands people can copy. Keep output honest and short.
- One blinking cursor per page at most. It stops under reduced motion.
- Don't: add macOS traffic-light dots, syntax-highlight with more than `term-accent`.

## Anatomy

```text
┌ div.np-term ─────────────────────────────────────┐
│ __bar           title             status         │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ __body          pre: .p prompt .c command .cur   │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Source: components/Terminal/README.md · Preview: components/Terminal/preview.html

# Textarea

A multi-line field in the Input box. Mono text, resizes vertically.

- Markup: inside `label.np-field`: `span.np-field__label`, `<textarea class="np-textarea">`, optional `span.np-field__hint`.
- Starts at 96px (four lines). Set `rows` for longer expected input.
- No › prompt: that belongs to single-line input.
- Errors: set `aria-invalid="true"` on the control and point `aria-describedby` at the hint's `id`, so the error is announced. The border, prompt and hint turn `alert`. `np-field--error` on the field still works for the look, but always add `aria-invalid` too.
- Disabled: `disabled` on the control. The box sinks to `paper-sunk` and the text mutes. Say why in the hint.
- Read-only: `readonly`, same as Input.
- Consumer provides: a label, a placeholder that shows the format (not a second label), and a length hint if there is a limit.

## Keyboard

- Tab focuses; Enter adds a line, so it never submits the form. Tab leaves the field.

Source: components/Textarea/README.md · Preview: components/Textarea/preview.html

---

# ThemeToggle

A two-state segmented control that switches between the Paper and Deep themes.

- Markup: `<div class="np-theme" role="group" aria-label="Theme">` with two `<button type="button" aria-pressed="false">` children: `data-set="light"` labelled "Paper" and `data-set="dark"` labelled "Deep".
- With no `data-theme` on `<html>`, the page follows the system setting (`prefers-color-scheme`). That is the default: don't set the attribute until the reader picks.
- Behaviour comes from `neptune.js`: a click sets `data-theme="light"` or `"dark"` on `<html>`, flips `aria-pressed` and saves the choice as `np-theme` in `localStorage`. On load, and when the system theme changes, it marks the side the page is actually showing.
- `neptune.js` is deferred, so also apply a saved choice in a one-line inline script in `<head>`, before the stylesheets, or the page flashes the wrong theme. Copy it from the preview.
- The pressed side fills `neptune`. Put it in `np-nav__actions`, after search.

## Keyboard

- Each side is a button: Tab between them, Enter or Space to choose. `aria-pressed` announces the current theme.

Source: components/ThemeToggle/README.md · Preview: components/ThemeToggle/preview.html

---

# Toast

A short machine message after something happens: dark like the terminal in both themes, mono, bottom right.

- Markup: one `section.np-toasts` per page with `aria-label="Notifications"` and `aria-live="polite"`, present from page load (empty). Add `div.np-toast` children: `p.np-toast__label` (`np-dot` + word), `p.np-toast__text`, `button.np-toast__close` ("Dismiss"), optional `div.np-toast__actions` with one `button.np-toast__action`.
- Variants: `np-toast--ok` (label `term-ok`), `np-toast--alert` (label `term-alert`, and `role="alert"` on the toast so it's announced at once). Default is neutral.
- Timing: ok and neutral toasts leave after 6s, paused while hovered or focused. Alert toasts stay until dismissed. A toast with an action stays until acted on or dismissed.
- Words: label is the result in one word (`Saved`, `Copied`, `Failed`); text is what happened, then what to do: "Deploy failed: missing `API_BASE_URL`. Set it in `.env`."
- At most three on screen; the oldest goes first. Newest at the bottom.
- Behaviour comes from `neptune.js`: Dismiss removes a toast, and `Neptune.toast({ kind, label, text, action })` adds one with the timing above (see the README's Behaviour section). Write toasts into the page yourself and they get Dismiss but no timer.
- Consumer provides: the region and the action handlers.
- Don't: toast something the user can see changed on the page, put the only copy of an error in a toast, or use a toast for a decision (use a Dialog). CodeCopy says "Copied" in its own button; no toast.

## Anatomy

```text
┌ section.np-toasts (live region) ───────────────┐
│ np-toast        __label ● word       Dismiss   │
│                 __text                         │
│                 __actions: one __action        │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Keyboard

- Toasts never take focus. Tab reaches Dismiss and the action in place; alert toasts are announced at once.
- An ok toast's timer pauses while it holds focus.

Source: components/Toast/README.md · Preview: components/Toast/preview.html

---

# Toc

The "on this page" list: the page's headings, the one in view marked with › in `neptune`.

- Markup: `<nav class="np-toc" aria-label="On this page">` with `p.np-toc__label` and `ol.np-toc__list`. Each `li` holds an `a` to a heading's id; add `np-toc__sub` to the `li` for an `h3`.
- Mark the heading in view with `aria-current="true"` on its link. Set it from an IntersectionObserver; with no script, mark none.
- Two levels: `h2` and `h3`. Deeper headings stay out.
- Lives in `np-docs__toc`, sticky; hidden below `bp-lg`.
- Consumer provides: the headings, in page order, with the same words as the headings.

## Anatomy

```text
┌ nav.np-toc ───────────────────────────────────────┐
│ __label         On this page                      │
│ __list          ol of links; np-toc__sub for h3   │
│                 › marks the heading in view       │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Keyboard

- Tab walks the headings; Enter jumps to one and moves focus there (the heading needs an `id`).

Source: components/Toc/README.md · Preview: components/Toc/preview.html

---

# Tooltip

A short mono hint on hover or keyboard focus, dark like the terminal.

- Markup: `span.np-tip` wrapping the trigger and `span.np-tip__bubble` with `role="tooltip"` and an `id`. The trigger gets `aria-describedby` pointing at that `id`. Add `np-tip--below` when there's no room above.
- Shows after 300ms on hover, at once on focus. Hovering the bubble keeps it open.
- Esc hides it without moving focus (WCAG 1.4.13); leaving the trigger resets it. That part comes from `neptune.js`; the delays are CSS.
- Consumer provides: one short sentence or a shortcut, under 80 characters: "Uses the last saved judge. About 4 min." or `⌘K`.
- Supplementary only. Touch screens have no hover, so nothing a reader needs may live only in a tooltip.
- Don't: put links or buttons inside, add one to a disabled control (it can't take focus; say why in a hint instead), or repeat the trigger's own label.

## Anatomy

```text
┌ span.np-tip ───────────────────────────────────┐
│ trigger         aria-describedby → bubble id   │
│ __bubble        role=tooltip, mono, term-bg    │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Keyboard

- Focus on the trigger shows it at once. Esc hides it; focus stays on the trigger.

Source: components/Tooltip/README.md · Preview: components/Tooltip/preview.html
